rules.statement: When new code stops reading or parsing at more than one condition, add a test for each stop condition, with input where content follows the stop point, and assert that the output holds only what comes before it.
rules.why: A test whose input ends where the section ends never runs the stop conditions, so if one breaks, the extra content slips into the output without any test failing.
rules.check: For a new function that stops scanning at a heading, a delimiter or similar marker, check whether any test input has content after each stop marker and asserts that the content is left out.

rules.statement: When code throws because a call to an external service failed, give the test stand-in for that service a switch that makes the call fail, and add a test that checks the run exits non-zero and that the error names what failed.
rules.why: Without that test, a regression that swallows the error passes the suite and leaves a half-done operation behind a green run.
rules.check: Look for new throw or exit-on-error paths after calls to external tools or APIs. Check whether the stand-in or fake can make that call fail, and whether a test asserts on the failure.

rules.statement: When code prints a warning only under some conditions, test both that it appears when it should and that it stays quiet in the cases that shouldn't trigger it, such as a project that is already updated.
rules.why: Tests that only check the warning appears would still pass after a regression that prints it for every input.
rules.check: For a new conditional warning, check whether the tests include a case for each condition that should keep it quiet and assert that no warning is printed.

rules.statement: A message shown to a user of generated or downstream code must say plainly when a file it points to belongs to another repository, such as the template's CHANGELOG.md, and not the reader's own project.
rules.why: A reader who looks for the file in their own project finds nothing.
rules.check: Look at warning and error text in tooling that runs in other projects. Find references like 'in its CHANGELOG.md' or bare file names that actually mean a file in the tool's own repository.
